citation: Steegen S.; Tuerlinckx F.; Gelman A.; Vanpaemel W. (2016). Increasing Transparency Through a Multiverse Analysis.
what_it_establishes: Data-processing choices can be represented as a multiverse of reasonable processed datasets and analyzed collectively rather than hiding one path.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not address eye-tracking measurement stages or HCI-specific gaze constructs.
positioning_role: General foundation for treating reasonable preprocessing alternatives as explicit uncertainty.

citation: Silberzahn R. et al. (2018). Many Analysts, One Data Set: Making Transparent How Variations in Analytic Choices Affect Results.
venue: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
what_it_establishes: Different expert teams can reach materially different numerical conclusions from the same research question and data through defensible analytic choices.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not isolate measurement uncertainty in eye tracking and is not a prespecified single-analyst measurement multiverse.
positioning_role: Motivates conclusion-level accountability for analytic decisions.

citation: Simonsohn U.; Simmons J.P.; Nelson L.D. (2020). Specification curve analysis.
what_it_establishes: Specification-curve analysis formalizes a justified specification set, graphical display of consequential decisions, and collective interpretation across specifications.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not prescribe which eye-tracking measurement dimensions are defensible or how raw gaze should be mapped to HCI constructs.
positioning_role: Methodological foundation for finite specification universes and decision-linked visualization.

citation: Liu Y.; Kale A.; Althoff T.; Heer J. (2021). Boba: Authoring and Visualizing Multiverse Analyses.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
what_it_establishes: Provides an integrated language and visual system for authoring and reviewing multiverse analyses and linking results to analytic decision spaces.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not address eye-tracking measurement validity, detector/AOI uncertainty, or a claim-centered gaze workflow.
positioning_role: Shows multiverse analysis is already an HCI/visual-analytics systems problem; novelty cannot rest on multiverse tooling alone.

citation: Sarma A. et al. (2023). multiverse: Multiplexing Alternative Data Analyses in R Notebooks.
what_it_establishes: Shows direct CHI interest in making alternative analyses authorable and inspectable within notebook workflows.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not provide an eye-tracking-specific measurement model or downstream claim-propagation study.
positioning_role: Positions the contribution as a measurement methodology for HCI rather than a new multiverse interface.

citation: Peelle J.E.; Van Engen K.J. (2021). Time Stand Still: Effects of Temporal Window Selection on Eye Tracking Analysis.
what_it_establishes: Across 8,281 visual-world time windows, reasonable temporal-window choices changed estimates and p-values and could reverse coefficient signs.
what_it_does_not_establish: Varies one temporal-selection family while holding the broader gaze measurement pipeline largely fixed.
positioning_role: Direct precedent that an eye-tracking analysis decision can alter substantive inference; narrows our contribution to cross-stage propagation.

citation: Godwin H.J.; Lee C.E.; Drieghe D. (2025). A multiverse analysis of cleaning and analyzing procedures of eye movement data during reading.
what_it_establishes: Evaluates 1,890 reasonable cleaning and analysis pipelines for a canonical reading effect, demonstrating that eye-movement research already has explicit multiverse analysis.
what_it_does_not_establish: Focuses on reading-data cleaning/analysis choices rather than a cross-stage raw-gaze measurement chain spanning geometry, detector, eye, AOI, quality, and downstream HCI process construction.
positioning_role: Critical novelty boundary: we must not claim multiverse analysis is new to eye tracking.

citation: Andersson R.; Larsson L.; Holmqvist K.; Stridh M.; Nyström M. (2017). One algorithm to rule them all? An evaluation and discussion of ten eye movement event-detection algorithms.
what_it_establishes: Ten event detectors produced substantially different event durations; fixation-detector rankings depended on evaluation method and stimulus context, making a single universal winner difficult to identify.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not propagate detector alternatives through one fixed substantive HCI coefficient and does not address the interaction with viewing geometry/AOI/quality choices.
positioning_role: Establishes event detection as a consequential measurement decision and supports avoiding detector-winner claims.

citation: Nyström M.; Holmqvist K. (2010). An adaptive algorithm for fixation, saccade, and glissade detection in eyetracking data.
what_it_establishes: Develops adaptive velocity-based event classification intended to reduce dependence on fixed thresholds and accommodate signal properties.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not remove all detector uncertainty or define a universal ground truth.
positioning_role: Algorithm-family background; reinforces that event representation is an explicit measurement model.

citation: Dar A.H.; Wagner A.S.; Hanke M. (2021). REMoDNaV: robust eye-movement classification for dynamic stimulation.
what_it_establishes: Provides open adaptive event classification validated on static/dynamic and lower-quality datasets; its analyses explicitly use stimulus geometry and viewing distance when interpreting gaze in visual-angle units.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not imply that REMoDNaV or any open detector is the correct representation for the SRL data; its dense-time-series requirements also introduce additional preprocessing decisions.
positioning_role: Supports detector generalization, geometry provenance, and the decision to keep unsupported resampling out of the frozen SRL denominator.

citation: Hessels R.S.; Kemner C.; van den Boomen C.; Hooge I.T.C. (2016). The area-of-interest problem in eyetracking research: A noise-robust solution for face and sparse stimuli.
what_it_establishes: AOIs for similar stimuli can vary in shape, size, and location; subjective AOI choices impede comparison and can change assignment under spatial noise.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not show that all AOI uncertainty materially changes every downstream statistical claim.
positioning_role: Establishes AOI geometry as a measurement decision that should be declared and, when ambiguous, audited.

citation: Holmqvist K.; Nyström M.; Mulvey F. (2012). Eye tracker data quality: what it is and how to measure it.
what_it_establishes: Defines and motivates explicit eye-tracker data-quality measurement, including accuracy and precision, as necessary for validity and comparability.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not prescribe one universal quality exclusion threshold or quantify downstream claim sensitivity to competing quality rules.
positioning_role: Supports treating quality as an explicit measurement dimension rather than invisible preprocessing.

citation: Orquin J.L.; Holmqvist K. (2018). Threats to the validity of eye-movement research in psychology.
what_it_establishes: Catalogues methodological threats across design, preprocessing, analysis, and interpretation and explicitly links common eye-tracking practices to validity concerns.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not provide a complete prespecified cross-stage multiverse for one substantive claim.
positioning_role: Broad validity rationale for treating the measurement pipeline as part of inferential design.

citation: Dunn M.J. et al. (2024). Minimal reporting guideline for research involving eye tracking (2023 edition).
what_it_establishes: Provides a community-developed minimum reporting checklist intended to improve reproducibility, critical appraisal, and comparability of eye-tracking methods/results.
what_it_does_not_establish: Reporting a chosen pipeline does not by itself quantify uncertainty across multiple defensible pipelines.
positioning_role: Separates our robustness contribution from reporting completeness: transparency is necessary but not sufficient for sensitivity evidence.

citation: Feit A.M.; Williams S.; Toledo A.; Paradiso A.; Kulkarni H.; Kane S.; Morris M.R. (2017). Toward Everyday Gaze Input: Accuracy and Precision of Eye Tracking and Implications for Design.
what_it_establishes: In an HCI gaze-input study, accuracy and precision varied strongly across users, targets, trackers, lighting, and screen regions, with direct implications for filters and interface design.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not test whether those measurement variations change a fixed inferential HCI coefficient.
positioning_role: HCI-specific evidence that gaze measurement properties are heterogeneous and consequential.

citation: Grootjen J.W.; Weingärtner H.; Mayer S. (2024). Uncovering and Addressing Blink-Related Challenges in Using Eye Tracking for Interactive Systems.
what_it_establishes: Shows that blink handling and associated preprocessing choices can affect eye-tracking data quality and accuracy in interactive-system research and proposes processing guidance.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not provide cross-stage claim robustness or justify one universal processing pipeline for all HCI studies.
positioning_role: Recent CHI-specific example that low-level preprocessing can be consequential for interactive eye tracking.

citation: Juřík V.; Juhaňák L.; Ružičková A.; Dostálová N.; Juříková Z. (2025). Experimental Dataset on Eye-tracking Activity During Self-Regulated Learning.
what_it_establishes: Documents the SRL dataset, Prompt/Non-prompt design, sample-level gaze, stimulus/AOI context, and historical BeGaze processing used by the primary case.
what_it_does_not_establish: Does not specify every downstream reconstruction decision needed for an open raw-to-claim robustness analysis; several geometry/event-provenance ambiguities required pre-result audit.
positioning_role: Empirical source for the complete-pipeline claim-propagation case, not the methodological novelty source.
